reasoning: A hybrid strategy combines autonomous feature comparison with validated XAI tools to reliably identify spurious features that are common across misclassified instances and have high attribution. This approach ensures both intuitive pattern recognition and statistically grounded attribution scores, improving confidence in detecting shared spurious correlations.

autonomous_tasks.query: Identify which features appear in all three misclassified instances (13590, 2021, 40175) and list their values across instances.
autonomous_tasks.expected_output: A list of shared features and their values in each instance

autonomous_tasks.query: Evaluate whether any shared feature (e.g., marital-status, education-num) has a semantically plausible connection to the target variable (>50K or <=50K) or is likely a spurious correlation based on domain knowledge.
autonomous_tasks.expected_output: A list of candidate spurious features with rationale for their lack of semantic relevance

tool_selection.reasoning: SHAP provides model-agnostic, consistent feature importance scores across instances, enabling detection of shared high-attribution features. LIME and Integrated Gradients help validate local importance and gradients, respectively. Sensitivity analysis quantifies impact when features are removed, confirming spuriousness. Together, these tools detect features that are both prevalent and influential despite lacking semantic relevance to class outcomes.
